content:
Google is set to limit the Gemini models available to free users and AI Plus subscribers following a usage-based pricing restructuring in May.

According to support documents updated this week, users of the Gemini App who do not subscribe to Google AI will only be able to use the (3.5) Flash-Lite model. From October 9, users who do not pay to use Gemini will no longer have access to (3.6) Flash or (3.1) Pro.

On the other hand, AI Plus subscribers will only be able to use Flash-Lite and Flash; Pro will no longer be offered. These users, who pay US$4.99 per month, will "receive an email explaining when the changes will take effect."

Gemini Model Google AI Plan Flash-Lite Flash Pro Without a plan ✓ X X AI Plus ✓ ✓ X AI Pro ✓ ✓ ✓ AI Ultra ✓ ✓ ✓

AI Pro and AI Ultra will not be affected. On the contrary, customers paying US$19.99 will be able to use the Deep Think option for "maximum parallel reasoning" capabilities, a feature currently limited to plans costing US$99.99 and US$199.99 per month.

AI Ultra version of Gemini 3.1 Pro with Deep Think capability

In October, the Gemini App also appears to be adding three computation intensity options — "Low," "Medium," and "High" — "applicable to all available models."

Currently, users can only enable the "Extended Thinking: Complex Problem Handling" feature. The three new computation intensity and thinking levels will align with the options offered in Google AI Studio and Antigravity.

It remains unclear how Gemini 4 Argon will be positioned. Google said earlier this week that Argon will be offered first to AI Ultra subscribers. The company has not indicated whether Argon will be classified as a Pro model or positioned as a new tier above Pro.
